custom_expected:
1. The panel comes back showing the same things you left in it. Nothing has been reset, cleared or reloaded from scratch - while it was hidden its contents were only out of sight, not thrown away.
2. The date you picked in the small month calendar is still the selected date.
3. The text you typed is still in the Search work orders box, and the list is still narrowed by it.
4. The list is still scrolled to roughly the position you left it at.
5. The panel comes back showing that work order's lines, not the full list of work orders - it returns to whichever of the two views was open when you hid it.
6. The work order you had opened is still the selected one.

Run this test as written and mark it on what you actually find. When it was last checked, on 11 August 2026, the Schedule toolbar had no panel button at all - the button furthest to the left above the grid was Today - so on that build steps 1 to 8 cannot be carried out and this test FAILS. Mark it failed if that is still what you see. If the button is there and behaves as described, mark it passed.
---

custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser, with the window at least 960 pixels wide.
2. Your role has the Schedule: View permission.
3. You are on the Schedule page and the left panel is showing.
4. There are enough work orders in the list that it has to be scrolled to see them all.
custom_steps:
1. In the small month calendar at the top of the left panel, click a date that is not today.
2. In the Search work orders box, type part of a customer name so that the list of work orders narrows.
3. Scroll the work order list down a little way.
4. Click one of the work order cards, so the panel swaps from the list of work orders to that order's list of lines.
5. Click the panel button above the grid, to the left of Today, to hide the left panel.
6. Click the same button again to show the panel.
7. Check each of the four things you set up in steps 1 to 4.

title: What you had set up in the left panel survives hiding and showing it
